Devon / Sarah —

Following up with technical recommendations for your evaluation and integration. High level guidance below; happy to expand on any point in the tech sync.

1) Recommended evaluation metrics- MRR@10 for single-click intents; NDCG@10 for graded relevance labels (recommended if you have 3-level labels); Precision@k (k=1,5) as a product-focused sanity check.
- For statistical confidence, run bootstrapped CIs and look at per-query deltas (median and interquartile range).

2) Pipeline suggestion (cost vs latency tradeoffs)- Stage 1: Embedding-based ANN to retrieve top-200 (cheap, sub-50ms typical with Faiss/HNSW).
- Stage 2: Reranker model on top-200 but only run on top-K candidates for strict latency: e.g., rerank top-50 for offline eval, top-10 for production P95.
- If you need <200ms P95, aim to rerank top-10 in production and use CPU-optimized or quantized reranker variants.

3) Reranker vs ranking API usage pattern- Redwood supports two common flows:
  a) /search/embed -> local ANN -> /models/rerank (candidate exchange). Rerank endpoint accepts a JSON payload: {"query":..., "candidates": [{"id":..., "text":...}, ...], "top_k": 10} and returns scored candidates.
  b) Direct /search/rerank that accepts query + corpus selector (if you want Redwood to do ANN+rerank end-to-end).

4) Top_k tuning rules of thumb- Start eval at top_k=50 (gives good oracle coverage for metrics). Compare production top_k choices (10 vs 20 vs 50) on MRR@10 and latency impact.
- Cost scales roughly linearly with top_k for the reranker stage; embeddings pre-filter cost is relatively fixed.

5) Structured output & tool-calling notes- If you want the reranker to return structured metadata (e.g., category tags, reason codes), use the structured output flag in the rerank API and provide a JSON schema. For tool-calling (e.g., call external catalog service for enrichment), we recommend doing enrichment offline in the candidate set prior to rerank to avoid additional call latency in the critical path.

6) Quick SDK/auth notes (Python)
- Use the Redwood Python client (pip install redwood-inference).
- Auth: create a scoped API key for staging (routes: rerank.read, rerank.eval).
- Example (pseudo):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="staging_XXX", region="us-west-2")
resp = client.rerank.reorder(query=query_text, candidates=candidate_list, top_k=10, structured=true)

7) Next operational steps- Please share a secure link to the sample candidate JSONL or give us temporary read-only S3 access.
- Let’s schedule a 30m tech sync Wed/Thu next week. Dev Patel will join to review routing/keys and help define the minimal production footprint.

If useful, we can also run a small pilot (2 weeks) with Redwood-managed evals and a performance summary.

Best,
